drivers.name: IntegrateIT UniFi Access
drivers.summary: Monitor one UniFi Access door and unlock it deliberately from Control4, over Ubiquiti's official local Developer API (HTTPS port 12445, customer-minted Bearer token). A configurable poll publishes DOOR_LOCKED, DOOR_POSITION, DOOR_NAME, and DEVICE_ONLINE variables and fires Door Opened/Closed, Door Locked/Unlocked, and Went Online/Offline events; remote unlock is double-gated behind the IntegrateIT license AND an explicit Allow Remote Unlock property. An access-convenience surface — not a life-safety system.
features: Official Ubiquiti local Developer API — HTTPS on the console, no cloud dependency
Door lock relay + door position (DPS) state polled and published as DOOR_LOCKED, DOOR_POSITION, DOOR_NAME, DEVICE_ONLINE
Door Opened/Closed, Door Locked/Unlocked, Went Online/Offline, and Remote Unlock Sent events for Composer programming
Remote unlock double-gated: IntegrateIT license AND the dealer-set Allow Remote Unlock switch — monitor-only out of the box
Unlocks are logged on the console under the API token's name (the documented default actor) — a truthful audit trail
List Doors action enumerates every door the token can see, flagging doors that cannot be remotely unlocked
LAN-only destination safeguard, self-signed-aware TLS with an opt-in strict mode, and the API token never written to the log

compatibility.label: Console
compatibility.value: UniFi console/gateway running the Access application, v1.9.1 or newer (not upgraded to Identity Enterprise — that removes the Developer API)

compatibility.label: Doors
compatibility.value: One door per driver instance; remote unlock needs the door bound to an Access hub

compatibility.label: State feedback
compatibility.value: Polled (default 5s); the documented WebSocket / webhook push channels are future work

requirements: A UniFi console running the Access application, reachable from the controller on port 12445
An API token minted by the console owner (Access > Settings > General > Advanced > API Token) with at least the view:space scope — plus edit:space if remote unlock will be used
The target door id (use the List Doors action to enumerate them)
For production, an IntegrateIT license key bound to this controller
limitations: Release Candidate: verified against the Control4 API simulator; acceptance on a physical UniFi console, Access hub, and door hardware is not yet attached to this release.

NOT A LIFE-SAFETY SYSTEM. This driver is an access-convenience surface — status, programming events, and a deliberate remote unlock. It must not be the sole control for any door where a failed, delayed, or replayed command has safety or security consequences; egress hardware and Access's own policies remain authoritative.

State feedback is by polling, not push: a badge-in, a manual unlock, or a door swing appears on the next poll (default 5s), not instantly. Ubiquiti's WebSocket notifications and webhooks are documented but out of scope for v0.1.0.

Remote unlock ships disabled. The Unlock Door command refuses until the dealer sets Allow Remote Unlock = Yes, and always requires a valid IntegrateIT license. Doors not bound to an Access hub cannot be remotely unlocked at all (a UniFi platform rule).
Doors without a wired position sensor (DPS) report position Unknown — Door Opened/Closed events never fire for them; lock relay state still works.

UniFi consoles serve a self-signed certificate on port 12445, so certificate verification is relaxed by default; set TLS Certificate Check = Require Valid Certificate after installing a real certificate on the console. Non-LAN console addresses are refused unless Allow WAN Console is explicitly set to Yes.
The Developer API is unavailable on consoles migrated to UniFi Identity Enterprise; one driver instance monitors exactly one door.

drivers.name: IntegrateIT UniFi Protect
drivers.summary: Surfaces UniFi Protect camera activity to Control4 programming over the official Protect Integration API (local HTTPS, X-API-KEY): camera inventory and per-camera reachability from GET /v1/cameras, plus motion, smart-detection (person / vehicle / package / animal), and doorbell-ring events read by polling the console's event feed. Events only — no video, no streams. LAN-only destination safeguard, the API key never logged, and MAC-locked IntegrateIT licensing.
features: Official Protect Integration API — local HTTPS with a customer-minted API key, no cloud dependency
Camera inventory: id, name, and connection state polled from the console and printed on demand
Motion Detected / Motion Ended events per camera for Composer programming
Smart detections: Person, Vehicle, Package, and Animal events, plus a generic Smart Detection event with LAST_SMART_TYPE
Doorbell Ring events from G4/G5 Doorbells
Camera Online / Camera Offline events on per-camera connection-state changes
Console Online / Console Offline reachability events and a CONSOLE_ONLINE variable
Watched Cameras filter to scope event firing to specific camera ids
LAN-only destination safeguard, the API key is never written to the log, and MAC-locked IntegrateIT licensing

compatibility.label: Console
compatibility.value: UniFi OS console running UniFi Protect with the Integration API (UNVR, UDM-Pro/SE, UCG, Cloud Key G2+)

compatibility.label: Protect version
compatibility.value: Protect releases publishing the Integration API v1 (spec v7.1.x); probed via GET /v1/meta/info

compatibility.label: Auth
compatibility.value: Console-scoped API key minted by the customer (UniFi OS → Control Plane → Integrations)

compatibility.label: Event feed
compatibility.value: Polled over HTTPS (default 3s); realtime WebSocket push is not implemented in v0.1.0

requirements: A UniFi OS console running UniFi Protect, reachable on the same LAN as the controller
The console's IP address (reserve it in DHCP) and an API key created in UniFi OS → Settings → Control Plane → Integrations
At least one adopted Protect camera; a G4/G5 Doorbell for ring events
For production, an IntegrateIT license key bound to this controller
limitations: Release Candidate: verified against the Control4 API simulator; acceptance on a physical UniFi console and cameras is not yet attached to this release.

Events only — this driver surfaces Protect activity to Control4 programming. It does not show video, provision RTSPS streams, take snapshots, or control cameras/PTZ. Navigator camera viewing is out of scope.

Event feed is POLLED, not pushed: Protect publishes motion/smart/ring events on a WebSocket subscription (GET /v1/subscribe/events); this version polls that endpoint over plain HTTPS on the configured interval instead of holding a WebSocket. Event latency is up to one poll interval, and consoles that answer the event path only after a WebSocket upgrade will reject the poll — the driver then reports it in Event Feed status, and camera-online/offline events (from GET /v1/cameras) keep working. Realtime WebSocket push is planned, not in v0.1.0.
Camera-offline detection derives from the console's reported per-camera connection state on the camera poll (default 30s), so it trails reality by up to one camera-poll interval.

The console's HTTPS certificate is self-signed; the driver skips TLS certificate verification by default (set Verify TLS Certificate = Yes only for consoles with a valid certificate). On very old OS builds without the modern URL API the legacy HTTP fallback cannot relax TLS verification and may fail against self-signed consoles.
The Site Manager cloud proxy path (api.ui.com) is not used — this driver is local-console only. Non-LAN console addresses are refused unless Allow WAN Console is explicitly set to Yes.
